themes_detail.label: Park Rule Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK, up 1500% from the 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.62), suggesting a sudden shift in park use patterns or enforcement visibility in Greenpoint/Williamsburg that warrants investigation into what specific violations are driving the spike.
evidence: 6 park rule violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
1500% increase with z-score of 11.62 (statistically significant anomaly)
No prior Reddit or media coverage explaining the spike, suggesting a newly emerging issue
reporting_angles: What specific park rules are being violated (alcohol, noise, hours, facilities misuse)?
Are violations concentrated in one park (McGolrick, East River State Park) or distributed?
Is this driven by new park use behavior post-winter or increased enforcement?

themes_detail.label: Wood Pile Dumping Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Wood pile complaints exploded to 5 LAST WEEK, up 3900% from the 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.74, highest severity spike), indicating either organized illegal dumping, construction debris mismanagement, or a specific environmental hazard accumulating in the district.
evidence: 5 wood pile complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
3900% increase with z-score of 14.74 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
1196 building permits filed in last 90 days (695 alterations, 191 new buildings, 24 demolitions) suggests active construction waste stream
reporting_angles: Is wood dumping concentrated near active construction sites (24 demolitions logged)?
Are complaints tied to a specific contractor or property owner dumping illegally?
What is the environmental/fire hazard risk of accumulated wood piles in residential areas?

themes_detail.label: Dirty Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints jumped to 102 LAST WEEK, up 244% from the 29.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.6), suggesting a sanitation infrastructure failure or acute cleanup lag affecting multiple blocks in the district.
evidence: 102 dirty condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 29.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Air quality complaints also UP 316% same week (13 vs. 3.1 avg), suggesting converging environmental issue
reporting_angles: Which neighborhoods/blocks are most affected by the dirty conditions (litter, debris, filth)?
Is this tied to street cleaning delays, construction debris, or rodent/pest activity?
Are sanitation workers striking, understaffed, or responding to the air quality/wood pile issues?

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints nearly quadrupled to 13 LAST WEEK, up 316% from the 3.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.8), overlapping with the wood pile and dirty conditions spikes and suggesting potential localized air pollution or burning.
evidence: 13 air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Convergence signal: dirty conditions (244% up) and wood piles (3900% up) same week suggest interconnected environmental event
reporting_angles: Are residents reporting burning (illegal fireworks, construction debris burning, arson)?
Is the air quality issue tied to the wood pile dumping or construction activity?
Has CGED or EPA monitored air quality in Greenpoint/Williamsburg during this spike period?

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 31 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 265% from the 8.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.82), suggesting a surge in Uber/Lyft congestion, illegal pickups, or unsafe driving in the district.
evidence: 31 for-hire vehicle complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 8.5 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Community board budget requests include 'improve traffic and pedestrian safety, including traffic calming' (repeated annual ask), indicating long-running transit concern
reporting_angles: Are complaints about blocking traffic, double parking, unsafe pickups, or congestion at specific hotspots?
Has rideshare activity increased near transit hubs (G train, waterfront?)
Are residents demanding more regulation or enforcement of for-hire vehicle rules?
